Scale_Evidence: Hawaiian controlled fishpond aquaculture was widespread; NPS notes an estimated 97 coastal fishponds on Oahu alone, and describes Hawaiian aquafarming as the most advanced among ancient Polynesian peoples.
Level_Rationale: LEVEL 2: multiple durable engineered installations across a major island group and a socially regulated fish-production system. The building is an abstraction: fishpond aquaculture is not literally a wharf.
Notes: The building gate is marine_chronometry, which HAW does not currently possess and which is not historically required for pond aquaculture. TECH_DISTRIBUTION_REVIEW=YES.

Scale_Evidence: Traditional Hawaiian salt was harvested not only from natural pools but on a larger scale in man-made shallow clay ponds; salt was important for preservation, voyages, ritual and medicine.
Level_Rationale: LEVEL 1: a durable, organized production technique with purpose-built evaporation ponds. Evidence supports a recognizable sector but not a large export industry by 1776.
Notes: No later nineteenth-century Puuloa export works are counted; the recommendation is for older Indigenous salt-pond production only.

Scale_Evidence: NPS documents a 175-mile corridor of ancient and historic trails on Hawaii Island alone, connecting more than 200 ahupuaa; prehistoric ala loa linked shorter coastal and mountain-ocean routes and included purpose-built surfaces through difficult lava terrain.
Level_Rationale: LEVEL 1: a genuine regional transport network exists, but it is a pedestrian/trail system rather than a wheeled turnpike system. Use the unified infrastructure building conservatively.
Notes: ROAD_LEVEL_JUSTIFICATION=YES (traditional road/trail network abstraction); CANAL_LEVEL_JUSTIFICATION=NO; mandatory pm_no_rail_network. No active rail in 1776.

Scale_Evidence: After first sustained European contact in 1767, Matavai became a repeatedly used provisioning anchorage. Cook returned in 1773; contemporary accounts describe a floating market involving around a hundred canoes exchanging fruit, fish and vegetables for imported goods, and formal rules regulated trade for provisions in 1769.
Level_Rationale: TRADE LEVEL 1 only: recurrent long-distance provisioning exchange was clearly established by the cutoff, but Tahiti was not yet a permanent international entrepot with warehouses or merchant houses.
Notes: TRADE_CENTER. Conservative seed only. Do not add building_port merely because Matavai was a favored anchorage.

Scale_Evidence: Cook and his officers in 1773 described Tongan canoes as exceptionally well built; a contemporary visit records a chief showing Cook a large double canoe still under construction in a boat-house. Construction quality was repeatedly singled out by the expedition.
Level_Rationale: LEVEL 1: organized specialist construction of large seagoing vessels under chiefly patronage is directly attested before the cutoff. Evidence supports a shipbuilding sector, not a European dockyard complex.
Notes: TNG currently lacks state_dockyard_systems. Historical canoe-building capacity is nevertheless attested, so keep the building recommendation and flag TECH_DISTRIBUTION_REVIEW=YES.
